notes.title: 2026 Question Set 14: Write Short Notes
notes.content:
(23) Development of communication in Brazil.             (July ’22)

Ans. (1) The landline phone services, mobile phone services, television and radio broadcasting, computer and internet facilities, etc. telecommunication services are well developed in Brazil.

(2) Today, nearly more than 45 per cent of Brazilian population has access to the internet facility.

(3) The central and the southern part of Brazil is densely populated. The modern telecommunication infrastructure is fairly developed in this region.

(4) The northern and western part of Brazil is sparsely populated. The communication infrastructure is comparatively limited in these regions.

(24) The main features of tourism in India.

Ans. (1) Tourism is one of the important occupations in India. Cultural and historical heritages, sculptures, clean seacoasts, national parks, bird sanctuaries, etc. have boosted the growth of tourism in India.

(2) Many foreign tourists visit India for exploring Indian heritage and culture, to carry our adventurous or business activities and to receive health services, etc.

(3) Since 2010, the number of international (foreign) tourists in India is remarkably constantly growing.

(4) There are plenty of opportunities for tourism at many places in India. Nowadays, ecotourism is promoted on a large scale in India.

(25) Importance of Standard time.

Ans. (1) If the country has a vast longitudinal extents, there will be a great difference between the time of its places located in the eastern and the western parts. In such countries, the importance of Standard time is the most.

(2) The Standard time of a country is its official time. It is commonly accepted at all places in a country.

(3) Standard time helps in making schedule of railways or airways.

(4) It also helps in coordinating the functioning of banks, schools, colleges, markets, hospitals located in various parts of a country.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 17: Give Geographical Reasons
notes.content:
(24) A dense network of railways has developed in the North Indian Plains.                                 (March ’19; July ’23)

Ans. (1) The North Indian Plains are low lying. There are not many hills in this region. The density of population in this region is quite high.

(2) The agriculture, trade, commerce, industries are well- developed in the North Indian Plains.

(3) The need for transport of goods as well as need of passenger transport is very high in this region. Therefore, a dense network of railways has developed in the North Indian Plains.

(25) Brazil attracts a lot of international tourists. (Sept. ’21)

Ans. Brazil attracts a lot of international tourists due to the following factors :

(1) White and clean sand beaches. (2) Attractive seacoasts.

(3) Beautiful islands. (4) Evergreen, deep, dense rainforests in Amazon river basin. (5) Variety of Animal and birds species.

(6) Gardens and Parks. (7) Cities like Brasilia, Rio de Janeiro, Sao Paulo, etc. (8) Manaus port and football stadium, etc.

(26) The waterways are not developed in Brazil. (March ’25)

Ans. (1) Most of the rivers in Brazil flow at high speed.

(2) The amount of total discharge of many rivers is very huge.

(3) In Brazil, rigid topography is found at many places near river basins. Many of the areas near rivers are inaccessible. Therefore, (internal) waterways are not developed in Brazil.

(27) Ecotourism is being developed more in Brazil. (March ’22 – ’23)

Ans. (1) Due to white sand beaches, scenic seacoasts, beautiful islands, evergreen dense forests, variety of species of birds and animals, gardens and parks, etc. tourism has increased in Brazil.

(2) Increased tourism may lead to pollution and environmental degradation. Therefore, it is necessary to control harmful effects of increased tourism.

(3) Promoting tourism as well as protecting environmental balance is equally essential. Therefore, ecotourism is being developed more in Brazil.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 19: Graph and Diagram Reading
notes.content:
Q. 12. Study the Figure (Graph) 9.1 given on page 61 and answer the following questions :

(1) What type of graph is shown here?

Ans. Multiple line graph is shown here.

(2) Which country attracted more international tourists in the year 1995?

Ans. India attracted more international tourists in the year 1995.

(3) In which country did more international tourists arrive in the year 2000?

Ans. More international tourists arrived in Brazil in the year 2000.

(4) In which year can an increase be seen in the number of international tourists in India?

Ans. An increase in the number of international tourists in India can be seen in the year 2010.

(5) What was the number of international tourists in the year 2015 in both the countries? What was the difference between them?

Ans. The number of international tourists was nearly 60 lakhs

in Brazil and was 130 lakhs in India. Thus, the difference between them was about 70 lakhs.

(6) What could be the reason of increase in tourists in India after the year 2010?

Ans. The professional outlook and increased facilities given to tourists could be the reason of increase in tourists in India after the year 2010.

Q. 13. Study the Figure (Graph) 9.2 given on page 61 and answer the following questions :                            (July ’23)

(1) What type of graph is shown here?

Ans. Joint bar graph is shown here.

(2) What does the graph show?

Ans. The graph shows contribution of tourism in GDP and percentage of population engaged in tourism.

(3) Which country’s tourism has a large share in the contribution towards GDP?

Ans. Brazil’s tourism has a large share in the contribution towards GDP .

(4) Which country has a larger population engaged in tourism sector but contributes lesser in GDP?

Ans. India has a larger population engaged in tourism sector but contributes lesser in GDP .

(5) In India, how much per cent is the contribution of tourism in its GDP?

Ans. In India the contribution of tourism in its GDP is 7.9 per cent.

(6) How much per cent of Brazilian population is contributing in its tourism industry?

Ans. 8.2 per cent of Brazilian population is contributing in its tourism industry.

Q.5(4): Give a geographical reason why telecommunications has become one of India’s fastest-growing sectors.
